source_snapshot.procedure: Use dd to fill files on all available E1.S/NVMe storage until full, then perform a warm reboot followed by a cold reboot.
source_snapshot.criteria: Approved storage reaches full condition without unexpected issue and the system completes both warm and cold reboot successfully while full.
source_snapshot.deepseek: CONFLICTING/UNSAFE; changes file filling into direct `/dev/nvme*` and `/dev/sd*` zero-overwrites of every discovered block device and requests unrelated IOmeter evidence.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: BLOCKED/CHANGED; correctly prohibits the raw-device loop but did not yet apply the approved storage-protection and safe-parameterization rules to construct a disposable-filesystem method.

old_problem: The active review was BLOCKED because DeepSeek's command would destroy every disk and the exact disposable filesystems, reserved control-plane space and recovery were absent. The Master explicitly says dd should fill files, not raw devices. ED-04 and the user-approved parameterization rule now provide a safe construction using only serial/UUID-bound disposable filesystems and regular files, with all protected storage excluded.
disposition_reason: GNU dd supports writing a named output file and synchronizing file data/metadata; no raw target is required. ED-04 forbids OS/mounted-protected/RAID/data-device guessing and confines writes to approved disposable mounts. ED-06 separates warm from cold reboot, ED-18 requires complete state transitions, ED-15 requires explicit fullness/boot/integrity oracles, and ED-17 preserves logs. IOmeter is a derived-package mismatch and is not substituted for the source dd method.
decision_basis: Directly read Compatibility row436 all 18 XLSX columns, same-row DeepSeek material, GPT V2/history3026, completed row435 LED baseline and adjacent next pending row437 PTAT memory case.
Applied the Master wording 'fill files': dd output is a regular file under each approved disposable mountpoint, never a block device, namespace, partition, RAID member or arbitrary discovered disk.
Applied GNU dd semantics for `of=<file>`, `conv=fsync` and `status=progress`; the expected terminal ENOSPC is recorded as the target state, not confused with an unexplained write failure.

Preserved 'all available' as all entries in an explicit project-approved disposable E1.S/NVMe filesystem matrix and retained separate warm reboot then full OFF-to-ON cold reboot while the filesystems remain full.
Directly read next formal queue Compatibility row437 and verified its manifest identity; no dd, storage fill, reboot, power cycle or DUT action ran.

test_case.test_name: Approved disposable E1.S/NVMe filesystem-full resilience across separate warm and cold reboots
test_case.purpose: Verify every approved noncritical disposable storage filesystem can reach its defined full/ENOSPC state using regular files and the platform remains bootable, manageable and data-consistent through distinct warm and cold reboot transitions.
required_package: Storage-owner-approved matrix of drive serial, controller/namespace, filesystem UUID, mountpoint and disposable test-file path for every in-scope E1.S/NVMe filesystem
Proof that targets exclude OS/boot/EFI, swap, RAID members, LVM/device-mapper backing devices, mounted protected/production data and shared control-plane/log filesystems
Backup/empty/disposable proof, pre-integrity hashes and guaranteed cleanup capacity/path
Project-approved full-state oracle, expected ENOSPC, inode/block reserve and separate root/log/control-plane free-space minimum
Approved warm-reboot and cold OFF-to-ON-to-OS-ready procedures, OOB console, boot deadlines and recovery plan
test_case.test_command: Resolve every target from the approved serial/filesystem-UUID/mountpoint matrix and re-prove exclusions before writing. On each disposable mount create only a uniquely named regular test file with a project-reviewed equivalent of `dd if=/dev/zero of=<approved_mount>/.sit_fullness_<id> bs=<approved_block> conv=fsync status=progress`, continuing only until that filesystem reaches its approved full/ENOSPC condition; never use `/dev/*` as `of=`. Record df/inode state, expected ENOSPC, service/control-plane reserve and file hashes. With target filesystems still full, execute the approved warm reboot through OS Ready and integrity checks, then separately execute the approved cold complete OFF-to-ON-to-OS-ready cycle and repeat checks. Remove only the recorded test files, sync, verify restored free space/data/health and retain all evidence.
test_case.expected_result: Every approved disposable target reaches the defined full/ENOSPC state through its regular test file while root, logs, OOB and control-plane reserves remain healthy. The warm reboot completes through OS Ready and all target identities/files remain consistent; the later cold OFF-to-ON cycle independently completes with the same integrity. Cleanup removes only test files and restores expected capacity without new storage, filesystem, kernel or SEL errors.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires the complete approved target/exclusion matrix, regular-file-only fill evidence for every in-scope filesystem, expected ENOSPC/full state, preserved control-plane reserve, separate successful warm and cold transitions, post-boot identity/integrity evidence and deterministic cleanup. Any raw-device write, guessed/all-discovered target, missing reserve, combined reboot claim or absent cleanup/recovery evidence is FAIL or INCONCLUSIVE—not PASS.
safety_gate: Never use a block/character device, partition, namespace node or unverified path as dd output; write only approved regular files on disposable filesystems
Revalidate OS/boot/EFI/swap/RAID/LVM/device-mapper/mounted-protected exclusions and control-plane reserve immediately before each file creation
Require storage-owner and reboot/power authorization with OOB observation before fill, warm reboot and cold cycle phases
Abort before service deadlock or reserve breach, preserve evidence, clean only known test files and never auto-retry a fill or reboot
expected_evidence: Backup/disposable proof, pre-integrity, root/log/control-plane reserve and exact dd commands
Per-filesystem transfer, expected ENOSPC/full df/inode state and service health
Independent warm-reboot and cold OFF/ON/OS-ready timelines with post-boot identity/integrity/log evidence
Exact test-file cleanup, restored free space, post-health and engineer verdict
test_case.recovery: On wrong target, reserve breach, service failure or reboot anomaly, stop writes/reboot progression, preserve OOB/filesystem/log evidence, delete only the recorded regular test files when safe, sync and restore the approved backup or filesystem state. Use the separately approved boot/power recovery path and do not repeat dd or either reboot automatically.

source_conflict.reason: The rewrite selects the Master dd-to-files method, rejects DeepSeek's raw all-device overwrite and treats unrelated IOmeter metadata as non-authoritative.

blocked.reason: ED-04 plus the Master file-filling wording establishes a safe regular-file method; exact disposable targets, reserves and reboot parameters are mandatory project configuration.

external_authorities.title: GNU Coreutils — dd invocation
external_authorities.applied_rule: Defines regular output files, transfer progress and fsync synchronization semantics used by the safe filesystem-level method.

external_authorities.title: systemd — reboot/poweroff
external_authorities.applied_rule: Distinguishes normal reboot and poweroff operations; project procedures must separately prove warm reboot and complete cold OFF/ON.

project_authority: The storage owner defines every in-scope disposable filesystem and protected exclusion; OS/power owners define reserves, warm reboot, cold OFF/ON and recovery. No discovered device is automatically in scope.
